problemStatement.formal: For n ≥ 2k+3: edgeCount G ≥ C(n-k-1,2) + C(k+2,2) + 1 → hasCycleOfLength G (n-k)
problemStatement.plain: Every graph on n ≥ 2k+3 vertices with at least C(n-k-1,2) + C(k+2,2) + 1 edges contains a cycle on n-k vertices. Moreover, such graphs are pancyclic from 3 to n-k.
whyMatters: Formalizes Erdős Problem #1012 on extremal graph theory
Connects Ore's Hamiltonian theorem, Bondy's pancyclicity, and Woodall's generalization
Establishes sharp edge thresholds for long cycle existence

proven: Woodall's pancyclicity: cycles of all lengths 3..n-k (axiom)
Threshold analysis: closed form, monotonicity, symmetry
